title: Emergency micro-hire pipeline and 90-day stabilization playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight, replicable playbook for filling urgent seat gaps ("micro-hires") and stabilizing the hire across the first 90 days. Use when: sudden attrition, product launch staffing gap, or short-term capacity needed while recruiting for a permanent role. Goal: hire someone who can be productive in 7–14 days and reach role-stable velocity by day 90.

Key constraints and principles:
- Keep interviews short and role-targeted: max 2 live interview loops + short take-home OR pair session.
- Prioritize measurable on-the-job tasks over broad cultural fit in the first pass.
- Default to 3-month contractor-to-perm conversion language where applicable to reduce offer friction.
- Assign a stabilization owner (usually manager or lead engineer) who runs 30/60/90 check-ins.

Urgent timeline (example):
Day 0–2: Requisition + brief role spec, hiring owner assigned, sourcing brief posted to channels (internal referrals, staffing partners, consumer job board).
Day 3–7: Screen 6–12 candidates (30m phone screens), shortlist 3–4.
Day 7–10: Two-interview loop (skills deep-dive + practical pairing/take-home). Offer issued same day if green.
Day 10–14: Start date (aim for start within 14 days of req).
Days 1–30: Tactical onboarding to get to baseline contributor tasks.
Days 31–90: Stabilization and knowledge-transfer to permanent owner, decision point for conversion or next steps.

Role spec template (short):
- Title: Micro-hire — [role] (contract 3 months, option to extend)
- Must-have skills: 2–3 bullet points (specific tech/stack and one collaboration/communication skill)
- First 14-day deliverable: clear, small scoped task (e.g., ship a monitoring alert, complete onboarding doc, triage three tickets)
- Reporting: direct to [manager] with weekly 1:1 + stabilization owner check-ins

Interview flow (minimal, repeatable):
1) 30-minute phone screen (recruiter or hiring owner): verify fundamentals, past similar short-term work, availability, and willingness to start quickly.
2) 60-minute technical pairing OR 48-hour take-home + 30-minute review. Focused rubric (see below).
3) Optional 30-minute cultural/working-style check with hiring manager for closing questions and logistics.

Rapid candidate rubric (scores 1–5, evaluator guidance):
- Role competency (weight 40%): can they complete the exact first-14-day deliverable? Look for examples of similar scoped work.
- Speed & triage (weight 20%): do they move quickly through unknowns and create pragmatic solutions?
- Collaboration (weight 20%): evidence of async communication, handoffs, and documenting work.
- Reliability & availability (weight 20%): can they commit to the timeline and show history of short-term wins.
Scoring guidance: 5 = demonstrable, recent, directly relevant; 3 = adjacent experience, some signal; 1 = no evidence. Pass threshold: weighted score >= 3.6.

Sample pairing session prompts (30–45 mins):
- "You have a production alert: pick the most pragmatic first 3 steps to mitigate user impact within 30 minutes."
- "Implement a small search/filter endpoint to return 5 sample items; focus on correctness and defensive checks."
Evaluation focuses on thought process, communication, and whether they finish the scoped task or demonstrate a clear path.

Offer structure recommendations:
- Base: market-competitive hourly/daily rate for contractors or prorated salary for permanent.
- Clear conversion checkpoint at day 75 with established metrics (see 90-day goals).
- Explicit variable: candidate must accept a short-term commitment with a defined handoff to permanent hiring pipeline.

Onboarding checklist (first 14 days) — manager & peer responsibilities:
Manager:
- Day 0: Intro email with 14-day deliverable and calendar of required meetings.
- Day 1: 30m role orientation + environment access verified (accounts, VPN, repo permissions).
- Weekly: 30m 1:1 + stabilization owner sync (first 4 weeks twice-weekly optional).
- Provide list of team docs to skim (runbook, architecture 10-minute read, nearest code owners).
Peers:
- Pair session scheduled within first 48 hours for the first deliverable.
- Buddy assigned for quick questions (buddy expected to respond within same business day).
People Ops:
- Confirm contract paperwork + payroll setup.
- Send welcome kit link and benefits summary where applicable.

30/60/90 stabilization metrics (objective examples):
- Day 30 (baseline contributor): completed first-14-day deliverable, merged at least one small PR, demonstrated environment fluency, documented 3 things learned.
- Day 60 (consistent owner): 3–4 medium tickets closed, can independently deploy a minor change, regular updates in standups, positive peer feedback.
- Day 90 (role-stable): full handoff to hiring owner; candidate meets conversion rubric (if considered), shows sustained throughput and code quality, has plan for longer-term growth.
Conversion rubric (yes/no checklist):
- Technical competency: meets role competency score >= 3.8 across evaluators.
- Reliability: attendance/availability >= 90% for scheduled windows.
- Culture & collaboration: peer feedback average >= 4/5 on working-style.
- Business fit: manager recommends conversion, budget approved by finance.

Stabilization owner play (how to run day 31–90):
- Weekly triage meeting (30m) to remove blockers and review blockers table.
- Knowledge-transfer sessions: 2–3 recorded sessions where permanent owner reviews architecture and product intent.
- Documentation handoff: micro-hire produces a 1-page "what I did" summary at day 60 and a final 2–3 page handoff doc at day 90.

Risk log (example triggers & mitigations):
- Candidate no-shows first week: mitigation = reassign buddy, reduce scope to critical tasks, escalate to recruiter for backup plan.
- Contractor availability drops: mitigation = re-prioritize deliverables, request overlapping overlap from candidate or hire short-term support.
- Performance below baseline: mitigation = 14-day improvement plan, documented expectations, consider termination if no progress.

Communication templates (short):
- Manager intro (Day 0): "Welcome [Name] — excited to have you. First 14-day deliverable: [X]. Calendar invites: daily standups, two pair sessions, weekly 1:1. Reach out to [buddy] if urgent."
- Offer summary (email): brief bullets: pay, start date, conversion checkpoint, required paperwork link, and who to contact for questions.

Minimal tracking sheet columns (for hiring owner or recruiter):
- Candidate, Source, Screen date, Pair date, Eval score, Offer status, Start date, Day-14 status, Day-30 status, Day-60 status, Day-90 decision.

Operational notes and heuristics (lessons learned):
- Keep the first deliverable customer-facing when possible — reduces ambiguity about success.
- Prefer candidates with prior short-term contractor or embedded squads experience.
- Timebox interviews strictly; long debates indicate higher permanent hiring intent and aren’t good for micro-hires.
- If conversion is likely, start permanent role requisition in parallel to avoid losing the candidate.

Open questions (to resolve in next revision):
- Budget guardrails for timezone overlap and overtime expectations.
- Legal language standard for contractor-to-perm conversion in EMEA.
- Staffing partner rates and SLAs for <7-day placements.

Appendix: quick scoring cheat-sheet (for interviewers)
- 5 (Excellent): Solved quickly, solid tests, communicated tradeoffs, direct match for deliverable.
- 4 (Good): Solved with minor gaps, good reasoning, would need 1–2 days ramp.
- 3 (Satisfactory): Adjacent experience, would need pairing and 1–2 weeks of monitoring.
- 2 (Weak): Partial understanding, missed key edge cases, high supervision needed.
- 1 (Insufficient): No usable signal for the scoped task.

Owner notes (Asha):
- This is intentionally compact. Use as the default for immediate operational gaps; iterate after the next two micro-hire runs.
- Please comment with any region-specific compliance blockers (Maya can coordinate legal).
